title: Semantic versioning
summary: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, pre-releases, and what a version number promises.

steps.title: What the numbers promise
body: | MAJOR | a breaking change: callers must change their code | removed an endpoint → `3.0.0` |
| MINOR | new, backwards-compatible features | added an optional field → `2.5.0` |
| PATCH | backwards-compatible bug fixes | fixed rounding → `2.4.2` |
Bumping a number **resets everything to its right** to 0: `2.4.1` + minor = `2.5.0`, not `2.5.1`.
`0.x.y` is special: anything may change at any time. `1.0.0` is your first stable promise.

steps.prompt: Current version `1.8.3`. Match each change to the next version.

steps.title: Pre-releases and build metadata
body: 2.0.0+build.57  ==  2.0.0   (after + is build metadata: ignored when comparing)
1. Compare MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH **numerically** (`1.10.0 > 1.9.0`, not alphabetically).
2. A version **with** a pre-release is lower than the same version without one.
3. Pre-release parts are compared dot by dot: numbers numerically, text ordinally, numbers before text; more parts wins if all else ties.

steps.prompt: Which list is sorted from lowest to highest?
steps.explain: Numeric comparison puts `1.9` below `1.10`, and a release candidate sits just below its release.

steps.prompt: A C# program compares versions the *wrong* way, as strings. What does it print?
steps.explain: As text, `'1'` < `'2'` < `'9'`, so `1.10.0` sorts first. This exact bug has shipped in real update checkers.

steps.prompt: Is the change breaking for consumers of a public REST API?
items: adding a new optional query parameter
making an optional request field required
changing a field from number to string
fixing a typo in an error message's text

steps.prompt: Tag a release so the pipeline publishes it.
steps.explain: An annotated tag marks the exact commit; pushing the tag triggers `on: push: tags: ['v*']`.

steps.title: Bump a version
prompt: Write `string Bump(string version, string part)` for plain `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` versions. `part` is `"major"`, `"minor"` or `"patch"`;
anything else throws `ArgumentException`. Remember to reset the numbers to the right.
hints: A switch expression with a `_ => throw` arm handles the bad input.

steps.title: Compare two versions
prompt: Write `int CompareVersions(string a, string b)` returning `-1`, `0` or `1`, following all three rules from the card,
and ignoring anything after `+`. A helper method is a good idea.
solution: for (int i = 0; i < Math.Min(ia.Length, ib.Length); i++)
bool na = int.TryParse(ia[i], out int x), nb = int.TryParse(ib[i], out int y);
int c = na && nb ? x.CompareTo(y) : na ? -1 : nb ? 1 : string.CompareOrdinal(ia[i], ib[i]);
hints: Split off `+...` first, then split at the first `-` into core and pre-release.
When the cores tie: no pre-release beats a pre-release. Then compare pre-release parts one by one.
For each part: both numeric → compare numbers; only one numeric → the numeric one is lower; both text → `string.CompareOrdinal`.
